Strand Coverage Imbalance (SCI) score

Source: R/strand-bias.R
sciStrandBias.Rd

Computes a strand bias score that normalises the per-site forward/reverse alternative-allele ratio by the global strand coverage ratio, making it suitable for amplicon data where strand coverage is inherently unequal. Mostefai et al. (2024) showed that strand bias filters which ignore this imbalance can discard genuine variants; their own metric is a per-strand binomial likelihood.

Usage

sciStrandBias(fwd_alt, rev_alt, fwd_total, rev_total)

Arguments

fwd_alt

Numeric vector. Forward-strand alternative allele read counts. All four count vectors must be numeric and hold non-negative, finite values or NA; NA marks a site with no call (see Details).

rev_alt

Numeric vector. Reverse-strand alternative allele read counts.

fwd_total

Numeric vector. Forward-strand total read counts.

rev_total

Numeric vector. Reverse-strand total read counts.

Value

A numeric vector of SCI scores (log2 scale). Values near zero indicate no strand bias; large absolute values indicate strand-specific enrichment or depletion.

Details

The SCI is defined as: $$\mathrm{SCI} = \log_2 \!\left( \frac{f_{\mathrm{alt}} / r_{\mathrm{alt}}} {F_{\mathrm{total}} / R_{\mathrm{total}}} \right)$$

where \(F_{\mathrm{total}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{total}}\) are the sums of forward and reverse total counts across all sites. A pseudocount of 1 is added to strand counts to avoid division by zero.

A site where any of the four counts is NA, as in a sample that made no call there, scores NA and is left out of the sums, so the global ratio is taken over the sites with all four counts.

References

Mostefai F et al. (2024). Refining SARS-CoV-2 intra-host variation by leveraging large-scale sequencing data. NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 6:lqae145. doi:10.1093/nargab/lqae145

Examples

sci <- sciStrandBias(
    fwd_alt   = c(50, 2, 30),
    rev_alt   = c(45, 40, 28),
    fwd_total = c(500, 500, 500),
    rev_total = c(480, 480, 480)
)
sci
#> [1]  0.09008968 -3.83136321  0.03744161
